adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members has no upper bound on params[:limit], letting an unauthenticated request pass ?limit=1000000 and force full serialization of every group user

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then executes `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serializes `members` into JSON. There is no upper bound/clamp on `limit`, so a request can supply an arbitrarily large `?limit=` and cause the server to load and serialize a very large number of users (potentially the whole group). While whether the request is unauthenticated depends on `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)` (not shown here), the unbounded `limit` itself is a real, verifiable performance/DoS risk introduced/left in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members passes params[:offset].to_i straight to .offset(), so a negative offset makes PostgreSQL raise 'OFFSET must not be negative' and return a 500

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then unconditionally applies it via `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping/validation to prevent negative values (unlike the JS side which clamps), so a request with `offset=-1` will pass a negative OFFSET to PostgreSQL, which raises an error (“OFFSET must not be negative”), resulting in a 500. This is a concrete correctness issue present in the changed code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) with an integer, causing ActiveRecord to raise RecordNotFound (500) when the user is not a member, where the old path was a silent no-op

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an integer. In ActiveRecord collection associations, `delete` accepts either records or primary key ids and removes the join rows; if the id is not currently associated (or even if no join row exists), it is typically a no-op and does not raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` because it does not need to `find` the record first. The diff also shows no explicit `find` call that would trigger `RecordNotFound` in the non-member case. Therefore the proposed finding's claimed 500 on “user not a member” is not verifiably introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb remove_member bypasses the Group#remove model API; users.delete uses delete_all for the has_many :through, skipping GroupUser callbacks and leaving the groups.user_count counter cache stale

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` was introduced and it removes membership via `group.users.delete(user_id)` (then `group.save`). Previously, membership changes in this controller went through `group.add(user)` / `group.remove(user)`, which is the model-level API intended to encapsulate membership logic. In Rails, `has_many`/`has_many :through` association `delete` typically removes rows from the join table using `DELETE`/`delete_all` semantics (i.e., without instantiating/destroying join records), which skips join-model callbacks and can bypass counter-cache maintenance that normally happens on `destroy`. Given this codebase clearly tracks `user_count` on groups (used widely in JS and serializers), deleting join rows this way risks leaving `groups.user_count` stale compared to using the model’s `remove` method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb create only reads name and visible, so the alias_level chosen in the new alias-level combo box for unsaved groups is silently discarded

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the client sends alias_level when creating a new group, but the server ignores it. In the diff, the group form always includes the alias level combo-box bound to `alias_level`, and the JS model’s `asJSON()` now returns `{ name, alias_level, visible }`, which `create()` POSTs directly to `/admin/groups`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` (no `alias_level` assignment). So any alias_level selected for an unsaved/new group will be silently discarded and the group will be created with the default alias_level.

The public group members page (routes/group-members.js.es6 + templates/group/members.hbs) now uses the paginated endpoint with a default limit of 50 but has no pagination controls, silently truncating non-automatic group members to the first 50

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit`/`offset` with a default `limit` of 50 (previously non-automatic groups returned the full member list). On the client side, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now sets the controller model to the group and calls `model.findMembers()` once, with no UI/actions added for changing `offset`/`limit`. The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` renders `{{#each m in members}}`, which will reflect only the first page loaded by `findMembers` (offset 0, limit 50). Unlike the admin group UI in this diff, the public group members page has no next/previous controls, so groups with >50 members will be silently truncated to the first 50.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb tests for .update, .add_members, and .remove_member hard-code id: 1 / group_id: 1 and depend on seed data ordering instead of using Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds/changes specs that call controller actions with hard-coded identifiers (e.g., `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, ...` and `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...`) and then assert against `Group.find(1)`. In these examples, the tests do not create a group with `id == 1` in the spec setup, so they implicitly rely on pre-existing/seeded automatic groups and a specific ID assignment. That makes the tests brittle and potentially incorrect in environments where group IDs differ or seed data isn’t present/loaded the same way. This is a verifiable issue present in the diff (test correctness/reliability problem).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb removed the 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' and 'succeeds silently when removing non-members' cases with no replacement, leaving the unknown-username branch of add_members and the non-member path of remove_member untested

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, the previous spec coverage under the old PATCH-based incremental update included explicit cases for (1) adding a non-existent username and expecting a silent success, and (2) removing a non-member and expecting a silent success. Those tests were removed along with the incremental update code. The new controller methods still contain analogous “no-op but succeed” branches: `add_members` skips usernames when `User.find_by_username` returns nil, and `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` which is a no-op if the user isn’t a member. The updated spec adds tests for successful adds and automatic-group restrictions, but does not add replacement tests covering these branches, so those paths are now untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec covers the new groups_controller.rb members response envelope {members:, meta: {total, limit, offset}}, the default limit, or offset behaviour, despite the JS depending on result.meta.total

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupsController#members` to return an envelope `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, and the JS (`Discourse.Group#findMembers`) now depends on `result.meta.total/limit/offset`. However, the proposed finding is purely about missing spec coverage (no tests added/updated to assert the new envelope/default limit/offset behavior). That absence is not a concrete runtime defect introduced by the diff; it’s a test-gap concern rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness problem in the implementation itself (and the implementation does include `meta`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb add_members calls params.require(:usernames).split(','), which raises NoMethodError (500 instead of 400) when a client posts usernames as an array

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. If a client submits `usernames` as an array (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`, which Rails will parse into an `Array`), `Array#split` does not exist and the action will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500. The diff contains no type check/coercion (e.g., `Array(usernames).join(',')`) and `require` only enforces presence, not type, so this failure mode is real and directly implied by the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb add_members issues one User.find_by_username query per name in the loop instead of a single User.where(username_lower: ...) batch query

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` followed by `User.find_by_username(username)`, which executes a separate SQL lookup per username. This is a verifiable N-queries-for-N-usernames pattern; batching with a single `User.where(...)` (e.g., on username_lower) would avoid the per-username query overhead.
